newsitem.title: USA: NEES expects to sell generation assets by end-1997.
newsitem.headline: NEES expects to sell generation assets by end-1997.

text.p: New England Electric System expects to sell its power generation assets before 1998, investor relations director Bob Seega said Wednesday.
"We think we can complete the sale of our generation business by the end of 1997," Seega said in a telephone news conference.
The company has retained Merrill Lynch and Co Inc to explore options for selling, spinning off or otherwise disposing of its generation assets, Seega said.
"We still believe outright sale of our generation business will obtain the highest value," he said.
NEES announced plans last month to divest its generation assets in order to focus on being a transmission and distribution company.

The company still needs regulatory approvals to go ahead with the plan. Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities agreed to issue a decision by Jan 10. NEES then plans to seek approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and other states.

Seega said the company expected to get a green light from FERC by mid-1997, after which NEES might have to apply to the Securities and Exchange Commission and Nuclear Regulatory Commission for further approvals.
"We believe the legislature does not have to formally approve our plan," Seega said, adding that regulatory approval should be enough.
But he said Massachusetts would have to pass legislation to open electricity markets to competition.
NEES plans to focus its business on transmission and distribution, both nationally and internationally, Seega said.
"The biggest opportunity that we see would be in expanding our distribution business -- merging or acquiring with another distribution company," he said.
He said NEES would look at expanding all over the United States, as well as seeking transmission opportunities in Paraguay, Uruguay, Brazil, and Tasmania.
The South American opportunities each would be worth $25 million to $50 million, but it was still unclear whether the projects would go ahead, Seega said.
He said building transmission, including high voltage direct current (HVDC) lines, is a "niche business for us."

"We're good at it. We've made money on it before, and... there are just not a lot of players out there," he said in a separate phone call, adding that, unlike other U.S. utilities, NEES was not looking to build power plants overseas.
The company is looking at the telecommunications business, Seega said.
NEES already leases out extra space it has on fiber optic lines, but he said it was "a fairly competitive low margin business at the moment."
